$comment: Canonical home: https://jseverino.com/schemas/cordon-checks-v3.json (the value of $id above) — the live, immutable URL this schema_version pins. The copy in the cordon repo at schema/cordon-checks-v3.json is the byte-identical development mirror; reference it for validation. v3 extends v2 (phase + unmet) with the autofix seam: a check row may carry status 'fixed' (it failed, a declared repair ran, and the RE-RUN passed — a fixed row is proven, never trusted), the top-level `fixed` array names those ids, and `repair` records what the repair did. Repairs run only under --fix; a plain run never mutates. checks/run.mjs --json is the reference emitter.
title: Cordon checks verdict (schema_version 3)

ok.$comment: The gate: true iff no check failed. A skipped check never fails the gate.

failed.$comment: ids of the failed checks — the same ids that appear in checks[].id with status 'fail'.

report.$comment: Relative path to the written failure report, or null when ok.

fixed.$comment: ids of checks repaired under --fix and proven green by a re-run — the same ids that appear in checks[].id with status 'fixed'. Always present; empty on a plain run (repairs only run under --fix). A fixed check never fails the gate, but it means the worktree changed: review and commit the repair.

phase.$comment: Where the check runs in the gate's ordering. Emitted only when a check declares one; absent means the engine's default (pre-build).

durationMs.$comment: The one runtime field — a verdict is a report, not a static description, so wall-clock cost is legitimately part of it. Everything else is deterministic: checks ride in registry/phase order, failed[] is derived.

effect.$comment: The check's own blast radius on cordon's ladder — the cost of producing this row, in the same vocabulary a command's --describe uses. A `command` entry (a spawned spec) carries the effect its registry entry declares.

unmet.$comment: The capabilities this check required but the environment did not satisfy (e.g. ['playwright'] not installed, ['macos'] wrong platform, ['built-dir'] no build output). Present ONLY on a skipped check, and only when the skip was capability-driven — an artifact simply being absent skips without it. Binary capabilities are open-ended names, so this is not a closed enum.

fix.$comment: Machine-readable remediation. The verdict-side mirror of effect: effect is the risk read before acting, fix is the remediation read after a failure. Required on a failed check.

rerun.$comment: The exact, deterministic command that reproduces this one check standalone. Required on a failed check.

detail.$comment: The failure's specifics — which link/line/path/output — the same text the human report folds in. Emitted on a failed check so an agent acts on the --json verdict without parsing the markdown report.

repair.$comment: What the repair was: an invariant's repair(ctx) summary, or the exact fix command a command entry spawned. Present only on a 'fixed' row — the audit trail for the mutation --fix made.

then.$comment: A failed check must carry its remediation: machine-readable fix + the deterministic command that reproduces it. The property shapes are defined on the check object above; they are restated here only so the requirement is self-contained under strict validation.

unmet.$comment: `unmet` is the capability-skip reason, so it can appear only on a skipped check.

repair.$comment: `repair` is the fixed-row audit trail, so it can appear only on a fixed check.
